question.prompt:
As shown in the figure below, point \(E\) lies in the opposite half-plane determined by line \(CD\) from point \(A\) so that \(\angle CDE = 110^\circ.\) Point \(F\) lies on \(\overline{AD}\) so that \(DE=DF,\) and \(ABCD\) is a square. What is the degree measure of \(\angle AFE?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q07_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
At \(D\), the three angles around the point are \(\angle CDE=110^\circ\), the square's \(\angle CDF=90^\circ\), and \(\angle EDF\). Hence
\[
\angle EDF=360^\circ-110^\circ-90^\circ=160^\circ.
\]
The given equality \(DE=DF\) makes triangle \(DEF\) isosceles. Its two base angles are each \((180^\circ-160^\circ)/2=10^\circ\). Since \(A,F,D\) lie on a line, \(\angle AFE\) supplements \(\angle DFE\). Therefore the requested angle is \(180^\circ-10^\circ=\boxed{170^\circ}\), choice D.
solutions.title: Angle sum around a point and isosceles base angles
